key_insight: A structure-preserving mixed finite element discretization of the intrinsic Hodges beam formulation enables explicit multibody dynamics without algebraic constraints while retaining exact energy behavior under suitable time integration.
engineering_relevance: This offers a cleaner and potentially more efficient way to simulate flexible beams and closed-loop multibody systems, especially when avoiding stiff DAE constraint enforcement is important.
method: Use the intrinsic beam equations with mixed finite elements so both kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions are imposed naturally.
Formulate interconnections without algebraic constraints, preserving a port-Hamiltonian structure for assembled multibody systems.
Combine the discretization with implicit midpoint integration to achieve exact energy preservation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on multiple examples, including closed kinematic loops, and notes fewer Newton iterations than existing energy-preserving schemes.
watch_item: Performance and robustness may depend on careful implementation of the mixed formulation and implicit midpoint solver, especially for large interconnected systems.
paper_title: Mixed finite element discretization of intrinsic geometrically exact beams for explicit multibody dynamics
